reasons: The best paid embedding choice is voyage-2, whose provider is local, which the factory does not handle.
Some providers such as cohere are not supported by the factory.
Scores, prices and license notes are hand-entered with no visible check or update date.

sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Open-source planning and reasoning models
sections.what: Describes several open-source models suited to planning and structured output, each with its strengths, memory needs, and license. These entries feed the default choices for planning work when no saved configuration exists.
sections.why: Gives the app a free option for planning tasks that can run on local hardware.
sections.watch_out: Hardware minimums are listed, so a machine below them will be slow or fail to load the model.

sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: Paid planning models from OpenAI
sections.what: Describes two paid OpenAI chat models with their prices, latency, quality scores and feature flags such as JSON mode. They are marked as recommended for planning and generation.
sections.why: Provides high-quality hosted options that need an OpenAI key.
sections.watch_out: Prices are fixed numbers that will drift from the provider's current pricing.

sections.name: File setup (part 3)
sections.title: Paid planning models from OpenAI (GPT-4o)
sections.what: Describes a faster, cheaper OpenAI model suited to generation and planning, with its prices and feature flags.
sections.why: Offers a cheaper alternative to the larger OpenAI model.
sections.watch_out: Scores and prices are estimates and may not match real performance.

sections.name: File setup (part 4)
sections.title: Paid models from Anthropic and Google
sections.what: Describes a Claude model and a Gemini model with their context sizes, prices and quality scores. Claude is marked as not supporting JSON mode, and the Gemini entry supports it.
sections.why: Gives the app paid options from two more providers with very large context limits.
sections.watch_out: The Claude entry says it does not support JSON mode, so requests that depend on JSON need the instruction approach instead.

sections.name: File setup (part 5)
sections.title: Generation and validation models
sections.what: Describes an open-source generation model, and a small open-source and a low-cost paid model for quick checks such as validation and sentiment. Each entry has suggested temperature and length settings.
sections.why: Matches cheaper, faster models to simpler jobs.
sections.watch_out: Suggested settings are only recommendations here and nothing in this file enforces them.

sections.name: File setup (part 6)
sections.title: Embedding models
sections.what: Describes open-source and paid embedding models, including a paid Cohere model and a Voyage model. These are the entries used when the app needs to turn text into numbers for search.
sections.why: Gives the app a choice of embedding models with different costs and quality.
sections.watch_out: The Voyage entry is marked with provider local while its description says it is an API service, and this mismatch can make it unusable.

sections.name: File setup (part 7)
sections.title: Emotion and sentiment models and more embeddings
sections.what: Describes two open-source emotion models and a further embedding entry from a different provider with a higher quality score. These cover detecting emotions in answers.
sections.why: Provides specialised models for emotion work.
sections.watch_out: The Voyage embedding entry has the highest quality score, so the best-paid lookup will pick it even though its provider cannot be built.

sections.name: File setup (part 8)
sections.title: Translation model
sections.what: Describes an open-source model that translates among about two hundred languages. Its license forbids commercial use.
sections.why: Gives the app a multilingual option for translation tasks.
sections.watch_out: The license is non-commercial, so using it in a paid product would break its terms.

sections.name: get_recommended_models_for_task
sections.title: Choosing models for a task
sections.what: Collects every catalog entry recommended for a given task, optionally limited to open-source or paid, and sorts them by quality score from highest to lowest.
sections.why: Gives the ordering logic that the model manager uses to pick defaults.
sections.watch_out: Only models marked as recommended for the task are considered, so a strong model not marked for it is never picked.

sections.name: get_best_open_source_model
sections.title: Best open-source model for a task
sections.what: Returns the top open-source model recommended for a task, or nothing if there is none.
sections.why: Gives a single default open-source choice when no saved configuration exists.
sections.watch_out: Returns nothing when no model fits, so callers must handle an empty result.

sections.name: get_best_paid_model
sections.title: Best paid model for a task
sections.what: Returns the top paid model recommended for a task, or nothing if there is none.
sections.why: Gives a single default paid choice when no saved configuration exists.
sections.watch_out: The top paid choice for embeddings is the Voyage entry, which the factory cannot build, so this default can break embedding setup.

summary: Holds a built-in catalog of AI models with their strengths, costs, quality scores and hardware needs, plus helper functions that pick the best model for a task.
purpose: Gives the app a ready list of models to recommend, so the owner does not have to research and enter each one.
why: Keeping the catalog as plain data makes it easy to add or change a model without changing logic.
how: The catalog is one large dictionary keyed by model name, grouped by task type. A helper gathers the models recommended for a task, sorts them by quality score, and keeps the top result. Two shortcuts pick the best open-source model or the best paid model for a task.
inputs: A task name such as planning, generation, validation, embedding, translation or emotion, and optionally a model type.
outputs: Lists or single entries of model details including provider, model identifier, quality score, and suggested settings.
risks: Scores and prices are hand-entered and will go out of date. Some entries use provider names the factory does not handle, and the voyage-2 entry is marked as local while its description says it is an API service.
debug: If a task picks an odd model, look at the quality scores for that task. If a provider fails to build, check the provider name in the entry. If a price looks wrong, check the date of the source page.
